verses.original: Καὶ παράγων εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον τυφλὸν ἐκ γενετῆς
verses.transliteration: Kai paragōn eiden anthrōpon typhlon ek genetēs
verses.literal: Now as Jesus was passing by He saw a man blind from birth
verses.literalPt: Jesus, ao passar, viu um homem cego de nascença.

verses.original: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες Ῥαββί τίς ἥμαρτεν οὗτος ἢ οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα τυφλὸς γεννηθῇ
verses.transliteration: kai ērōtēsan auton hoi mathētai autou legontes Rhabbi tis hēmarten houtos ē hoi goneis autou hina typhlos gennēthē
verses.literal: and His disciples asked Him . . . Rabbi who sinned this man or his parents that he was born blind
verses.literalPt: Perguntaram-lhe seus discípulos: Mestre, quem pecou para que este homem nascesse cego? Ele ou seus pais?

verses.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Οὔτε οὗτος ἥμαρτεν οὔτε οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ ἀλλ’ ἵνα φανερωθῇ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Apekrithē Iēsous Oute houtos hēmarten oute hoi goneis autou all’ hina phanerōthē ta erga tou Theou en autō
verses.literal: Jesus answered Neither this man nor his parents sinned but this happened so that the works of God would be displayed in him
verses.literalPt: Respondeu Jesus: Nem ele pecou, nem seus pais, mas isso se deu para que as obras de Deus nele sejam manifestas.

verses.original: ἡμᾶς δεῖ ἐργάζεσθαι τὰ ἔργα τοῦ πέμψαντός με ἕως ἡμέρα ἐστίν ἔρχεται νὺξ ὅτε οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐργάζεσθαι
verses.transliteration: hēmas dei ergazesthai ta erga tou pempsantos me heōs hēmera estin erchetai nyx hote oudeis dynatai ergazesthai
verses.literal: While it is daytime we must do the works of Him who sent Me Night is coming when no one can work
verses.literalPt: É necessário que façamos as obras do que me enviou, enquanto é dia; vem a noite, quando ninguém pode trabalhar.

verses.original: ὅταν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ὦ φῶς εἰμι τοῦ κόσμου
verses.transliteration: hotan en tō kosmō ō phōs eimi tou kosmou
verses.literal: While I am in the world I am the light of the world
verses.literalPt: Estando eu no mundo, sou a luz do mundo.

verses.original: Ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἔπτυσεν χαμαὶ καὶ ἐποίησεν πηλὸν ἐκ τοῦ πτύσματος καὶ ἐπέχρισεν αὐτοῦ τὸν πηλὸν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς
verses.transliteration: Tauta eipōn eptysen chamai kai epoiēsen pēlon ek tou ptysmatos kai epechrisen autou ton pēlon epi tous ophthalmous
verses.literal: When Jesus had said this He spit on the ground made some mud - and applied it to the man’s eyes
verses.literalPt: Tendo assim falado, cuspiu no chão e, fazendo lodo com o cuspo, aplicou-o aos olhos do cego,

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ὕπαγε νίψαι εἰς τὴν κολυμβήθραν τοῦ Σιλωάμ ὃ ἑρμηνεύεται Ἀπεσταλμένος ἀπῆλθεν οὖν καὶ ἐνίψατο καὶ ἦλθεν βλέπων
verses.transliteration: kai eipen autō Hypage nipsai eis tēn kolymbēthran tou Silōam ho hermēneuetai Apestalmenos apēlthen oun kai enipsato kai ēlthen blepōn
verses.literal: Then He told him Go wash in the Pool of Siloam (which means “Sent” So the man went and washed and came back seeing
verses.literalPt: dizendo: Vai lavar-te no tanque de Siloé (que quer dizer, Enviado). Ele foi, lavou-se e voltou com vista.

verses.original: Οἱ οὖν γείτονες καὶ οἱ θεωροῦντες αὐτὸν τὸ πρότερον ὅτι προσαίτης ἦν ἔλεγον Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ καθήμενος καὶ προσαιτῶν
verses.transliteration: Hoi oun geitones kai hoi theōrountes auton to proteron hoti prosaitēs ēn elegon Ouch houtos estin ho kathēmenos kai prosaitōn
verses.literal: At this his neighbors and those who had formerly seen . . . . . . him begging began to ask Isn’t . . . this the man who used to sit and beg
verses.literalPt: Então, os vizinhos e os que dantes o conheciam de vista, como mendigo, perguntavam: Não é este o que se assentava para mendigar?

verses.original: Ἄλλοι ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Οὐχί ἀλλὰ ὅμοιος αὐτῷ ἐστιν Ἐκεῖνος ἔλεγεν ὅτι Ἐγώ εἰμι
verses.transliteration: Alloi elegon hoti Houtos estin alloi elegon Ouchi alla homoios autō estin Ekeinos elegen hoti Egō eimi
verses.literal: Some claimed that he was but others said No he just looks like him But the man kept saying I am the one
verses.literalPt: É ele mesmo, respondiam uns; não é, mas é parecido com ele, diziam outros. Porém ele dizia: Sou eu mesmo.

verses.original: Ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ Πῶς οὖν ἠνεῴχθησάν σου οἱ ὀφθαλμοί
verses.transliteration: Elegon oun autō Pōs oun ēneōchthēsan sou hoi ophthalmoi
verses.literal: How then were your eyes opened they asked
verses.literalPt: Perguntaram-lhe, pois: Como te foram abertos os olhos?

verses.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ἐκεῖνος Ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰησοῦς πηλὸν ἐποίησεν καὶ ἐπέχρισέν μου τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς καὶ εἶπέν μοι ὅτι Ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν Σιλωὰμ καὶ νίψαι ἀπελθὼν οὖν καὶ νιψάμενος ἀνέβλεψα
verses.transliteration: Apekrithē ekeinos Ho anthrōpos ho legomenos Iēsous pēlon epoiēsen kai epechrisen mou tous ophthalmous kai eipen moi hoti Hypage eis ton Silōam kai nipsai apelthōn oun kai nipsamenos aneblepsa
verses.literal: He answered The man they call Jesus made some mud and anointed my eyes and He told me to go to Siloam and wash So I went and washed and received my sight
verses.literalPt: Respondeu ele: Aquele homem chamado Jesus fez lodo, ungiu-me os olhos e disse-me: Vai a Siloé e lava-te; então, fui, lavei-me e fiquei vendo.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ποῦ ἐστιν ἐκεῖνος Λέγει Οὐκ οἶδα
verses.transliteration: Kai eipan autō Pou estin ekeinos Legei Ouk oida
verses.literal: Where is He they asked I do not know he answered
verses.literalPt: Eles lhe perguntaram: Onde está ele? Respondeu: Não sei.

verses.original: Ἄγουσιν αὐτὸν πρὸς τοὺς Φαρισαίους τόν ποτε τυφλόν
verses.transliteration: Agousin auton pros tous Pharisaious ton pote typhlon
verses.literal: They brought to the Pharisees the man who had been blind
verses.literalPt: Levaram aos fariseus o que fora cego.

verses.original: ἦν δὲ σάββατον ἐν ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ τὸν πηλὸν ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἀνέῳξεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς
verses.transliteration: ēn de sabbaton en hē hēmera ton pēlon epoiēsen ho Iēsous kai aneōxen autou tous ophthalmous
verses.literal: Now the day on which Jesus had made the mud and opened his eyes was a Sabbath
verses.literalPt: Ora, era sábado o dia em que Jesus fez lodo e lhe abriu os olhos.

verses.original: πάλιν οὖν ἠρώτων αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πῶς ἀνέβλεψεν Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πηλὸν ἐπέθηκέν μου ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς καὶ ἐνιψάμην καὶ βλέπω
verses.transliteration: palin oun ērōtōn auton kai hoi Pharisaioi pōs aneblepsen Ho de eipen autois Pēlon epethēken mou epi tous ophthalmous kai enipsamēn kai blepō
verses.literal: So the Pharisees also asked him how he had received his sight - The man answered . . . He put mud on my eyes and I washed and now I can see
verses.literalPt: Então, os fariseus, por sua vez, perguntaram-lhe como recebeu a vista. Ele respondeu: Aplicou lodo aos meus olhos, lavei-me e agora vejo.

verses.original: Ἔλεγον οὖν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων τινές Οὐκ ἔστιν οὗτος παρὰ Θεοῦ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὅτι τὸ σάββατον οὐ τηρεῖ Ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον Πῶς δύναται ἄνθρωπος ἁμαρτωλὸς τοιαῦτα σημεῖα ποιεῖν Καὶ σχίσμα ἦν ἐν αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: Elegon oun ek tōn Pharisaiōn tines Ouk estin houtos para Theou ho anthrōpos hoti to sabbaton ou tērei Alloi de elegon Pōs dynatai anthrōpos hamartōlos toiauta sēmeia poiein Kai schisma ēn en autois
verses.literal: Because of this some of the Pharisees said This man is not from God for He does not keep the Sabbath But others said How can a sinful man perform such signs And there was division among them
verses.literalPt: Por isso, alguns dos fariseus diziam: Este homem não é de Deus, porque não guarda o sábado. Outros, porém, diziam: Como pode um homem pecador fazer tais milagres? Havia dissensão entre eles.

verses.original: λέγουσιν οὖν τῷ τυφλῷ πάλιν Τί σὺ λέγεις περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἠνέῳξέν σου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν ὅτι Προφήτης ἐστίν
verses.transliteration: legousin oun tō typhlō palin Ti sy legeis peri autou hoti ēneōxen sou tous ophthalmous Ho de eipen hoti Prophētēs estin
verses.literal: So once again they asked the man who had been blind What do you say about Him since it was your eyes He opened He is a prophet - the man replied
verses.literalPt: Tornaram a perguntar ao cego: Que dizes tu a respeito dele, visto que te abriu os olhos? É profeta, respondeu ele.

verses.original: Οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἦν τυφλὸς καὶ ἀνέβλεψεν ἕως ὅτου ἐφώνησαν τοὺς γονεῖς αὐτοῦ τοῦ ἀναβλέψαντος
verses.transliteration: Ouk episteusan oun hoi Ioudaioi peri autou hoti ēn typhlos kai aneblepsen heōs hotou ephōnēsan tous goneis autou tou anablepsantos
verses.literal: The Jews still did not believe - that the man had been blind and had received his sight until . . . they summoned his parents
verses.literalPt: Mas os judeus não acreditaram que ele tivesse sido cego e que tivesse recebido a vista, enquanto não chamaram os pais dele

verses.original: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτοὺς λέγοντες Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς ὑμῶν ὃν ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι τυφλὸς ἐγεννήθη πῶς οὖν βλέπει ἄρτι
verses.transliteration: kai ērōtēsan autous legontes Houtos estin ho huios hymōn hon hymeis legete hoti typhlos egennēthē pōs oun blepei arti
verses.literal: and asked . . . . . . Is this your son the one you say was born blind So how is it that he can now see . . .
verses.literalPt: e os interrogaram: É este vosso filho, que vós dizeis ter nascido cego? Como, pois, vê agora?

verses.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν οὖν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπαν Οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς ἡμῶν καὶ ὅτι τυφλὸς ἐγεννήθη
verses.transliteration: Apekrithēsan oun hoi goneis autou kai eipan Oidamen hoti houtos estin ho huios hēmōn kai hoti typhlos egennēthē
verses.literal: His parents answered . . . . . . We know he is our son and we know he was born blind
verses.literalPt: Responderam seus pais: Sabemos que este é nosso filho e que nasceu cego;

verses.original: πῶς δὲ νῦν βλέπει οὐκ οἴδαμεν ἢ τίς ἤνοιξεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἡμεῖς οὐκ οἴδαμεν αὐτὸν ἐρωτήσατε ἡλικίαν ἔχει αὐτὸς περὶ ἑαυτοῦ λαλήσει
verses.transliteration: pōs de nyn blepei ouk oidamen ē tis ēnoixen autou tous ophthalmous hēmeis ouk oidamen auton erōtēsate hēlikian echei autos peri heautou lalēsei
verses.literal: But how he can now see . . . - or who opened his eyes we do not know Ask him He is old enough to speak for himself
verses.literalPt: mas como agora vê não sabemos; ou quem lhe abriu os olhos nós não sabemos. Interrogai-o, já tem idade; ele mesmo falará por si.

verses.original: Ταῦτα εἶπαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἐφοβοῦντο τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ἤδη γὰρ συνετέθειντο οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἵνα ἐάν τις αὐτὸν ὁμολογήσῃ Χριστόν ἀποσυνάγωγος γένηται
verses.transliteration: Tauta eipan hoi goneis autou hoti ephobounto tous Ioudaious ēdē gar synetetheinto hoi Ioudaioi hina ean tis auton homologēsē Christon aposynagōgos genētai
verses.literal: His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews For the Jews had already determined that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue
verses.literalPt: Isso disseram seus pais, porque tinham medo dos judeus, porquanto estes já tinham combinado que, se alguém confessasse ser Jesus o Cristo, fosse expulso da sinagoga.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ εἶπαν ὅτι Ἡλικίαν ἔχει αὐτὸν ἐπερωτήσατε
verses.transliteration: dia touto hoi goneis autou eipan hoti Hēlikian echei auton eperōtēsate
verses.literal: That was why . . . his parents said He is old enough Ask him
verses.literalPt: Por isso, disseram seus pais: Ele já tem idade; interrogai-o.

verses.original: Ἐφώνησαν οὖν τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐκ δευτέρου ὃς ἦν τυφλὸς καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Δὸς δόξαν τῷ Θεῷ ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: Ephōnēsan oun ton anthrōpon ek deuterou hos ēn typhlos kai eipan autō Dos doxan tō Theō hēmeis oidamen hoti houtos ho anthrōpos hamartōlos estin
verses.literal: So a second time they called for the man who had been blind and said . . . Give glory to God We know that this man is a sinner
verses.literalPt: Então, chamaram pela segunda vez o homem que fora cego e lhe disseram: Dá glória a Deus; nós sabemos que este homem é pecador.

verses.original: Ἀπεκρίθη οὖν ἐκεῖνος Εἰ ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν οὐκ οἶδα ἓν οἶδα ὅτι τυφλὸς ὢν ἄρτι βλέπω
verses.transliteration: Apekrithē oun ekeinos Ei hamartōlos estin ouk oida hen oida hoti typhlos ōn arti blepō
verses.literal: He answered Whether He is a sinner I do not know There is one thing I do know I was blind but now I see
verses.literalPt: Ele respondeu: Se é pecador, não sei; uma coisa sei: eu era cego e agora vejo.

verses.original: Εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ Τί ἐποίησέν σοι πῶς ἤνοιξέν σου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς
verses.transliteration: Eipon oun autō Ti epoiēsen soi pōs ēnoixen sou tous ophthalmous
verses.literal: What did He do to you they asked How did He open your eyes
verses.literalPt: Perguntaram-lhe, pois: Que é o que te fez? Como te abriu os olhos?

verses.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς Εἶπον ὑμῖν ἤδη καὶ οὐκ ἠκούσατε τί πάλιν θέλετε ἀκούειν μὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς θέλετε αὐτοῦ μαθηταὶ γενέσθαι
verses.transliteration: Apekrithē autois Eipon hymin ēdē kai ouk ēkousate ti palin thelete akouein mē kai hymeis thelete autou mathētai genesthai
verses.literal: He replied I already told . . . you and you did not listen Why do you want to hear it again Do you also want to become His disciples
verses.literalPt: Ele lhes respondeu: Já vo-lo disse e não ouvistes; por que quereis ouvir outra vez? Porventura, quereis também vós tornar-vos seus discípulos?

verses.original: Καὶ ἐλοιδόρησαν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπον Σὺ μαθητὴς εἶ ἐκείνου ἡμεῖς δὲ τοῦ Μωϋσέως ἐσμὲν μαθηταί
verses.transliteration: Kai eloidorēsan auton kai eipon Sy mathētēs ei ekeinou hēmeis de tou Mōuseōs esmen mathētai
verses.literal: Then they heaped insults on him and said You are His disciple we are disciples of Moses
verses.literalPt: Injuriaram-no e disseram: Discípulo dele és tu; mas nós somos discípulos de Moisés.

verses.original: ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι Μωϋσεῖ λελάληκεν ὁ Θεός τοῦτον δὲ οὐκ οἴδαμεν πόθεν ἐστίν
verses.transliteration: hēmeis oidamen hoti Mōusei lelalēken ho Theos touton de ouk oidamen pothen estin
verses.literal: We know that God spoke to Moses but we do not know where this man is from
verses.literalPt: Nós sabemos que Deus falou a Moisés, mas este não sabemos donde ele é.

verses.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἐν τούτῳ γὰρ τὸ θαυμαστόν ἐστιν ὅτι ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε πόθεν ἐστίν καὶ ἤνοιξέν μου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς
verses.transliteration: Apekrithē ho anthrōpos kai eipen autois En toutō gar to thaumaston estin hoti hymeis ouk oidate pothen estin kai ēnoixen mou tous ophthalmous
verses.literal: That is remarkable indeed the man said . . . . . . . . . - You do not know where He is from and yet He opened my eyes
verses.literalPt: Respondeu-lhes o homem: É maravilhoso que não saibais donde ele é; contudo, ele me abriu os olhos.

verses.original: οἴδαμεν ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς ἁμαρτωλῶν οὐκ ἀκούει ἀλλ’ ἐάν τις θεοσεβὴς ᾖ καὶ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιῇ τούτου ἀκούει
verses.transliteration: oidamen hoti ho Theos hamartōlōn ouk akouei all’ ean tis theosebēs ē kai to thelēma autou poiē toutou akouei
verses.literal: We know that God does not listen to sinners but He does listen to the one who worships Him and does His will
verses.literalPt: Sabemos que Deus não ouve a pecadores; mas, se alguém temer a Deus e fizer a sua vontade, a este ele ouve.

verses.original: ἐκ τοῦ αἰῶνος οὐκ ἠκούσθη ὅτι ἠνέῳξέν τις ὀφθαλμοὺς τυφλοῦ γεγεννημένου
verses.transliteration: ek tou aiōnos ouk ēkousthē hoti ēneōxen tis ophthalmous typhlou gegennēmenou
verses.literal: Never before has anyone heard of opening the eyes of a man born blind
verses.literalPt: Desde que há mundo, nunca se ouviu que alguém abrisse os olhos a um cego de nascença.

verses.original: εἰ μὴ ἦν οὗτος παρὰ Θεοῦ οὐκ ἠδύνατο ποιεῖν οὐδέν
verses.transliteration: ei mē ēn houtos para Theou ouk ēdynato poiein ouden
verses.literal: If this man were not from God He could do no such thing
verses.literalPt: Se esse homem não fosse de Deus, nada poderia fazer.

verses.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ἐν ἁμαρτίαις σὺ ἐγεννήθης ὅλος καὶ σὺ διδάσκεις ἡμᾶς καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω
verses.transliteration: Apekrithēsan kai eipan autō En hamartiais sy egennēthēs holos kai sy didaskeis hēmas kai exebalon auton exō
verses.literal: They replied . . . . . . . . . You were born in utter sin and you are instructing us And they threw him out
verses.literalPt: Eles lhe replicaram: Tu nasceste todo em pecados e tu nos estás ensinando? E lançaram-no fora.

verses.original: Ἤκουσεν Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω καὶ εὑρὼν αὐτὸν εἶπεν Σὺ πιστεύεις εἰς τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου
verses.transliteration: Ēkousen Iēsous hoti exebalon auton exō kai heurōn auton eipen Sy pisteueis eis ton Huion tou anthrōpou
verses.literal: When Jesus heard that they had thrown him out He found the man and said Do you believe in the Son of Man
verses.literalPt: Soube Jesus que o haviam lançado fora e, encontrando-o, lhe perguntou: Crês tu no Filho do Homem?

verses.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ἐκεῖνος καὶ εἶπεν Καὶ τίς ἐστιν Κύριε ἵνα πιστεύσω εἰς αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Apekrithē ekeinos kai eipen Kai tis estin Kyrie hina pisteusō eis auton
verses.literal: Who is He Sir he replied . . . . . . Tell me so that I may believe in Him
verses.literalPt: Quem é ele, Senhor, para que eu creia nele? — respondeu-lhe o homem.

verses.original: Εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Καὶ ἑώρακας αὐτὸν καὶ ὁ λαλῶν μετὰ σοῦ ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: Eipen autō ho Iēsous Kai heōrakas auton kai ho lalōn meta sou ekeinos estin
verses.literal: You have already seen Him Jesus answered - He is the One speaking with you
verses.literalPt: Disse-lhe Jesus: Já o viste, e é ele quem fala contigo.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ ἔφη Πιστεύω Κύριε καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Ho de ephē Pisteuō Kyrie kai prosekynēsen autō
verses.literal: Lord I believe - he said And he worshiped Jesus
verses.literalPt: Ele disse: Creio, Senhor; e o adorou.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἰς κρίμα ἐγὼ εἰς τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον ἦλθον ἵνα οἱ μὴ βλέποντες βλέπωσιν καὶ οἱ βλέποντες τυφλοὶ γένωνται
verses.transliteration: Kai eipen ho Iēsous Eis krima egō eis ton kosmon touton ēlthon hina hoi mē blepontes blepōsin kai hoi blepontes typhloi genōntai
verses.literal: Then Jesus declared For judgment I have come into this world so that the blind may see and those who see may become blind
verses.literalPt: Jesus prosseguiu: Eu vim a este mundo para um juízo, a fim de que os que não veem vejam; e os que veem se tornem cegos.

verses.original: ἤκουσαν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων ταῦτα οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄντες καὶ εἶπον αὐτῷ Μὴ καὶ ἡμεῖς τυφλοί ἐσμεν
verses.transliteration: Ēkousan ek tōn Pharisaiōn tauta hoi met’ autou ontes kai eipon autō Mē kai hēmeis typhloi esmen
verses.literal: Some of the Pharisees who were with Him heard this and they asked Him Are . . . we blind too
verses.literalPt: Ouvindo isso alguns dos fariseus que estavam com ele, perguntaram-lhe: Porventura somos nós também cegos?

verses.original: Εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἰ τυφλοὶ ἦτε οὐκ ἂν εἴχετε ἁμαρτίαν νῦν δὲ λέγετε ὅτι Βλέπομεν ἡ ἁμαρτία ὑμῶν μένει
verses.transliteration: Eipen autois ho Iēsous Ei typhloi ēte ouk an eichete hamartian nyn de legete hoti Blepomen hē hamartia hymōn menei
verses.literal: If you were blind Jesus replied you would not be guilty of sin But since you claim you can see your guilt remains
verses.literalPt: Respondeu-lhes Jesus: Se fôsseis cegos, não teríeis pecado algum; mas agora dizeis: Nós vemos, fica subsistindo o vosso pecado.
